notes.meaning: God's arm has not lost any of its strength, and He is still fully able to save His people. His ears are not dull or hard of hearing either. If prayers seem unanswered, the problem is not that God has grown weak or tired of listening.

The real barrier between the people and God was their own continuous wrongdoing. Their sins had formed a thick dividing wall, cutting off their fellowship with Him and blocking His blessings. Because they persisted in rebellion, the Lord hid His face and refused to hear their cries.

The prophet points out the terrible crimes that caused this separation. Their hands were stained with innocent blood, and their fingers were busy committing injustices. Their mouths were just as guilty, constantly speaking outright lies and muttering hateful words against others.

No one in the community stood up to defend what was fair, and lawsuits were filed on dishonest grounds. People based their dealings on empty arguments and deceit rather than the truth. They spent their time planning trouble in their minds, just like carrying a child, and then brought evil deeds to life.

The evil schemes of these corrupt people are compared to snake eggs and cobwebs. Anyone who gets involved in their toxic plans faces spiritual ruin and death, just like eating poison. Even if someone tries to stop or break their plans, more danger and malice hatch out.

Just as spiderwebs are far too thin to make real clothes, human schemes cannot hide human guilt before God. Self-made plans and good works can never cover up sin the way God's true righteousness does. Instead of providing genuine help, these worthless works only bring violence and harm.

Sinners ran eagerly toward evil deeds, hurrying to shed innocent blood without any hesitation. Their inner thoughts were continually occupied with wicked plans, leaving destruction and heartbreak in their path. The Apostle Paul later quoted these words in Romans to show that every human being is broken by sin.

Those who chase after sin have no experience with real peace, whether with God, with others, or in their own hearts. They choose twisted, dishonest paths instead of fair and honest living. Anyone who walks down those crooked roads will never find true peace and safety.

The prophet steps forward to speak for the nation, honestly confessing why rescue had not arrived. Because the people refused to treat others with justice, God held back His delivering help from them. They kept waiting for the bright light of relief, but they were left walking in heavy gloom.

The people felt completely blind and helpless, groping along a blank wall to find a way out of their miseries. Even in the middle of the day, when things should have been clear, they stumbled as if it were pitch black. While others around them flourished, they felt abandoned and as good as dead.

Their deep sorrow broke out in different ways as trouble dragged on. Some showed their anger by growling loudly like hungry bears, while others wept softly with the mournful cooing of doves. They longed for fair treatment and salvation, but deliverance stayed far away because of their guilt.

The people stopped blaming the Lord and frankly admitted their massive pile of sins. Their evil choices stood before God as clear witnesses proving their guilt beyond any doubt. They could no longer hide from their crimes, because their consciences knew every one of them.

The confession lists the specific ways the nation had broken faith with God. They had openly rebelled against Him, broken His covenant, and walked away from His leadership. Toward their neighbors, they plotted cruel oppression in their hearts and spoke outright lies.

Courts of law and public meeting places had lost all sense of fairness and integrity. Justice was pushed completely out of the way, and uprightness was kept standing far off outside the courtroom. Truth had stumbled and fallen in the city square, and honest dealings were not allowed through the door.

Honesty had vanished so thoroughly that anyone who refused to join in evil became an easy target for wicked people to rob. The Lord watched this terrible injustice unfold among His own people, and it greatly displeased Him. He saw that no one in authority was doing anything to set things right.

The Lord was astonished to find no human leader willing to defend truth, and no intercessor praying to turn away judgment. Since no human being could or would fix the problem, God decided to step into action all by Himself. His own strong arm brought salvation, and His own righteousness gave Him the strength to finish the work.

God is described as an armed warrior dressing for battle to save His people and defeat their oppressors. His perfect justice covers Him like armor, and His certain salvation crowns His head like a helmet. He wraps Himself in garments of payback and wears a cloak of fiery zeal to defend His holy name.

The Lord will hand out exact retribution to everyone based on what they have done. He will bring His fierce judgment against His foes, whether they are wicked rebels at home or heathen nations in distant coastlands. No enemy is too far away for God's justice to reach and repay.

God's awesome judgments will cause people all over the earth, from sunrise to sunset, to revere His holy name. Even when evil surges in like a raging flood, the Spirit of the Lord will raise a defense and drive the enemy away. God's mighty display of power will draw nations from everywhere to worship Him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars translate the second line to describe the Lord Himself coming like a pent-up river driven along by the wind of God, rather than an enemy coming in like a flood.

notes.meaning: The Lord promises that a Redeemer—a family rescuer who buys back what was lost—will come to Zion to deliver His people. This glorious rescue is promised to those who turn away from their evil deeds in true repentance. The Apostle Paul points to this promise in Romans 11 to describe the spiritual salvation of Israel through Christ.

differ.view: This promise refers primarily to the end times, when ethnic Israel as a nation will turn from sin and welcome Jesus as the Messiah.

notes.meaning: The Lord seals His promises by giving an everlasting covenant to His redeemed people. He promises that His Holy Spirit and the message He has placed in their mouths will never depart from them. This life-giving Word will be passed down from parents to children and grandchildren forever.
